newsitem.title: UK: BOE to include gilt repo in money mkt ops.
newsitem.headline: BOE to include gilt repo in money mkt ops.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Wednesday it plans to include gilt repo in its daily money market operations and extend widely the number of eligible counterparties.
It hopes the changes will take place from early 1997.

In a consultative paper, the Bank said it would also seek to simplify late lending arrangements, moving the time to 1530 GMT from around 1440 GMT at present, and offer the arrangement to settlement banks only.
Late help would be offered at 1/4 percent above the Bank's repo rate.
The Bank said the changes were purely technical and would have no impact on policy.

"These proposals relate to the mechanics of the Bank's day-to-day operations...they do not alter the Bank's basic approach to implementing monetary policy by managing short-term interest rates through open market operations," it said in a statement.
It said the changes are consistent with the direction and spirit of proposals under discussion at the European Monetary Institute.

The Bank is seeking comments on its proposals by January 10 1997, and said it hopes to then issue a definitive paper setting out the changes, with a view to introducing the new operations in "the early months of 1997, if possible".
Following is a summary of the key changes laid out in the Bank's paper entitled "The Bank of England's operations in the sterling money markets"':
-- the Bank will continue to use Treasury bills and eligible local authority and bank bills in its daily money market operations, along with operations in gilt repo;
-- the Bank seeks to broaden the range of counterparties able to participate and invited banks, building societies and securities firms to contact it if they are interested;
-- the afternoon round of open market operations will be moved to 1440 GMT from 1400 GMT at present;

-- new late lending will take place at 1530 GMT, and be offered to settlement banks only. It is intended for only shortages unforeseen at the time of BOE afternoon operations and the rate offered will be 1/4 percent above the Bank's repo rate. For a transitional period , a similar facility will continue for discount houses;
-- banks must still balance their settlement accounts with the Bank at the end of each day;
-- the Bank will end its twice monthly gilt repo facility;
-- counterparties need not be separately capitalised or specialist entities. GEMMs no longer required to be separately capitalised.

Ian Plenderleith, executive director at the Bank, said these will be the most dramatic changes in its operations this century. "We hope the changes will keep our operations in the mainstay of market developments in London and enhance the scope of (banks) to manage their day-to-day activity," he said.
He added bringing UK operations into line with those being discussed by EMI "was not the main motive" in introducing them.

The Bank's proposals are designed to take account of the successful development of the gilt repo market, which has grown steadily since its introduction in January 1996. It stood at 60 billion stg outstanding by August, with daily turnover of 15 billion stg.
Plenderleith said he expected the changes would not damage the seven discount houses which have, in recent years, diversified their business away from pure money market dealing.
